newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sidanko bond, share issue to consolidate units.
newsitem.headline: Sidanko bond, share issue to consolidate units.

text.p: Russian oil group Sidanko, caught in a fight for production unit Purneftegaz, said on Monday it would issue convertible bonds to consolidate shares of its subsidiaries into the parent company.
Shareholders at an extraordinary meeting on Saturday approved issuing a convertible bond and raising authorised capital to 26.17 billion roubles from 9.30 billion as part of a share conversion plan.
The bonds were not intended to raise capital, a Sidanko spokesman said.
"It was decided the issue of bonds (convertible into shares of AO Sidanko) would be the mechanism to convert shares of subsidiaries into shares of AO Sidanko," a company statement said.
The board of directors would have to work out details of the planned conversion and bond issue, including conversion rates for shares in various subsidiaries, the spokesman said.

OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sidanko) is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil companies created during early market reform of the industry after the breakup of the Soviet Union.
Sidanko, one of Russia's largest oil producers, has a number of operating units including Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil has already converted shares in its subsidiaries into the parent company, and another large group, Surgutneftegaz, is working on a similar project.

But Sidanko is unlikely to pursue the conversion plan while it is caught up in a battle over another production unit, Purneftegaz, which both Sidanko and state-controlled AO Rosneft oil company claim.
"Resolving the issue with Purneftegaz will open the possibility to work out the conversion issue," the spokesman said.
"While the situation with Purneftegaz is not decided, no one will make a decision on the other issue."
A Russian court will take up the issue of Purneftegaz, which government agencies had awarded independently to both Sidanko and Rosneft, at the end of January.
But the process could draw out much longer, the spokesman said. A separate court last week ruled that the operating unit would remain under Rosneft's control until the issue had been settled.

The Purneftegaz agreement could also overshadow a tender for 51 percent of Sidanko because the Federal Property Fund, which is organising the tender, said Sidanko's assets included the 38 percent stake, or 51 percent of voting shares, of Purneftegaz.
The offer, for which bids currently are being accepted, closes on January 9.
